identity: Arabic simplified/abridged children's retelling of Louisa May Alcott's Little Women (the sisters Meg, Jo, Beth, Amy; the mother Marmee; the father away at the war; the book they read is Pilgrim's Progress = مسرحية السائح المسيحي). Graded-reader narrative prose covering chapter one (مسرحية عيد الميلاد) and the opening of chapter two (الفصل الثاني / عيد ميلاد سعيد), including three standalone heading paragraphs. Register is plain modern standard Arabic: third-person perfective narration alternating with heavy direct speech. The defining surface habit is the FRONTED DIALOGUE TAG (قالت/صاحت/تنهدت/تأففت/أضافت/استطردت/أومأت/اندفعت + name) followed immediately by the quoted words: the punctuation stripped after such a tag was a colon plus quotation marks, NOT a full stop, so tag and speech are ONE sentence.
law: The sentence unit is one complete predication, and this corpus joins predications by two opposed devices. (1) ASYNDESIS = FULL STOP: when a finite clause abuts another finite clause with no connective at all, a period stood there. This is the single most reliable cue in the document and it fires in narration (دقت الساعة السادسة تماما | وضعت بيث خف والدتها) and inside speech alike (لدي فكرة | لنشتري جميعا هدايا). (2) CONNECTIVE = NO STOP: و / ف / لكن / بل / ثم / إذ / حتى / لذا normally coordinate WITHIN one sentence, and a long parallel list of sister-actions strung on و is one sentence (ذكت جو النيران بالحطب وأعدت ميج العشاء وساعدتها بيث وأشرفت إيمي). THREE OVERRIDES beat rule (2). (a) A switch between quoted speech and narration is ALWAYS a boundary even when the next word carries و, because the closing quotation mark forced a stop (...وقد استنفدت كل ما لدي من مال | وأخرجت زجاجة العطر الجديدة من الحقيبة). (b) A change of illocution inside one speech turn is a boundary, because the stripped ? or ! ended the sentence (...تحظين بوقت ممتع | هل أمضيتن يوما سعيدا). (c) و followed by a FRONTED adverbial that restarts the narrative clock (وبعد دقائق قليلة, وبعد مرور نصف ساعة) or that opens a new topic (وهناك رسالة خاصة, وعلى الرغم من أن) begins a new sentence. A fronted temporal clause (عندما... / بعد أن... / في صباح يوم...) is a sentence OPENER here, never a tail on the previous sentence; the document does this at least seven times. The dialogue tag never separates from its speech. Heading paragraphs are one unit each. CALIBRATION: the resulting sentences run 2-28 tokens, mean about 13; any parse that yields a 39- or 46-token sentence has a missed boundary in it.
reasoning: Site 113 (معا): Beth's quoted line ends at ...ولطالما كنا معا and بدا أن كلماتها أسعدت شقيقاتها is the narrator's comment, not her words: speech/narration switch, boundary. Sites 142/156/161: Meg's speech is three asyndetic complete predications, then وبالرغم مما قالته ميج returns to narration, so 161 is a boundary despite the و. Site 294 (غيابه), the hardest و-site: leaving وفكرت ميج attached yields a 39-token sentence, far outside this document's 2-28 range, and Jo's insistence and Meg's thought are two separate deliberations. Split, med. Sites 201/691/867 (أما بيث فقد / أما إيمي فقلدت / أما بيث فقد): I went back and forth twice. AGAINST splitting: أما is a coordinator and each case is the middle member of an enumeration of sisters. FOR splitting: the three unsplit readings land at 26, 29 and 29 tokens, i.e. all three simultaneously at the very ceiling of the observed length range, which is too neat to be chance, and each أما switches the actor after an already complete predication. I split all three at med, and I flag them AS A BLOCK as the likeliest place I am wrong: if the key disagrees, it will disagree on all three at once. Site 634 (الخياطة) versus 642 (المطبخ), a genuine attachment ambiguity: بعد أن حملت هانا الخادمة الصحون إلى المطبخ can either close the sewing sentence or open the reminding sentence. I attach it FORWARD to ذكرت السيدة مارمي because this document opens sentences with fronted temporal clauses repeatedly and never leaves one dangling at the end. Med. Site 791 (ماهرة): أترون يا فتيات كم أن ميج ماهرة is interrogative, so a question mark closed it even though فلنسر على خطاها opens with ف; same logic as the confident site 436. Sites 505 (خطاب) and 918 (أمنا): exclamatory speech runs, لا بد أنه خطاب | يعيش أبي and لقد حضرت أمنا | خبئا السلة: asyndetic and distinct speech acts. Site 915 (أسرعا) REJECTED: I considered making the one-word command its own sentence but read it as an interjection fused to the announcement that follows; too weak to claim. Site 511 (أجل) REJECTED: a one-word yes is more often comma-joined than period-joined, so I split only at 515 (أبيكن) where هو بخير starts asyndetically. Site 1135 (كثيرا): the three-sister و-list would otherwise be 32 tokens, above the ceiling; وكانت ميج تغطي بالفعل is a backgrounded kana+participle state distinct from the two preceding perfectives, so I split there rather than at 1124. Sites 210, 366, 495, 623, 682, 697, 858 and 1124 all REJECTED as و-internal coordination: each leaves a sentence of 14-25 tokens, comfortably inside range, so nothing forces a split. Sites 1047/1053/1059/1074 in Marmee's untagged all-speech paragraph are four clean asyndetic utterances (greeting | exclamation | announcement | description) closing with the question هل من الممكن. Mechanical checks performed: no boundary sits on an <NL>; every token immediately before an <NL> plus the final token 1177 is present and marked hi; two self-caught index slips were corrected, namely 867 (الهدايا) not 868 (أما), and a dropped 716 (كله) that had left a 46-token run.
